confirmed.title: Complex-symmetry justification for the circular-contour variant contradicts the code: feast_region uses the sesquilinear form W^H H W, which uses no complex symmetry
confirmed.evidence: Paper: "The circular-contour variant departs from the two-sided scheme of Kestyn et al.: because $H(\theta)$ is complex symmetric, its left and right invariant subspaces coincide up to conjugation, so a single right subspace with an orthogonal Rayleigh--Ritz projection and an explicit residual gate replaces the biorthogonal left-right pair. It is the methodological contribution of this work." The premise is correct (for H=H^T, Hx=lambda x implies H^H conj(x)=conj(lambda) conj(x)), but its consequence is that the two-sided reduction collapses to the BILINEAR form W^T H W, which is itself complex symmetric. feast.py:128 computes the opposite: `Hr = W.conj().T @ H @ W`, i.e. W^H H W, followed by feast.py:129 `lam, Vr = np.linalg.eig(Hr)`, the general non-Hermitian solver. W^H H W is the ordinary one-sided Galerkin projection, valid for ANY matrix, complex symmetric or not; it produces a non-symmetric Hr and would give exactly the same code for a fully general H. Complex symmetry is therefore nowhere exploited, and the single-subspace reduction is the standard construction of contour-integral eigensolvers for general matrices (Sakurai-Sugiura / Beyn / non-Hermitian FEAST), not a modification derived here. The sole substantive difference between feast_region and feast_interval in the released code is: complex trial block (feast.py:109), no `np.real(Q)` projection, `np.linalg.eig` instead of `eigh`, and a center off the real axis. This is the paper's headline novelty claim and it is an overclaim as written.
confirmed.fix:
Keep the code exactly as released (it is correct; do NOT apply the reviewer's fix (a), which fails to converge). Fix the prose so it describes what the code does, and restore the honest novelty claim that the 15-page version already had.

confirmed.title: No "explicit residual gate" exists in feast_region; the residual is only a stopping test, identical in kind to the variant the table classifies as unchanged
confirmed.evidence: The paper presents "an explicit residual gate" as one of the two ingredients that "replaces the biorthogonal left-right pair". In feast_region the residual is computed at feast.py:134 and used at one place only, feast.py:136-137 `if res.max() < tol: return`, i.e. a convergence/stopping criterion. Eigenvalue selection is purely geometric: feast.py:131 `inside = np.abs(lam - center) < radius`. Nothing is rejected on residual grounds, and if max_iter is exhausted the eigenvalues are returned regardless (feast.py:141). The real-interval variant, which Tab. 2 classifies as "Implemented here from the published algorithm, unchanged", does exactly the same thing (feast.py:79-82), so the "gate" is not even a distinguishing feature of the circular variant. The caller stores the residual (run_resonances.py:150, written to E6_resonances.csv) but never rejects on it.
